data.narrative:
Profluent, a Seed-stage biotech company founded by Ali Madani, is evaluated within a Biotech & Health sector comp universe of 3 public peers (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private comparables, including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals. The company has raised $150M to date.

One valuation method proved applicable to this analysis. Stage-progression modeling uses a $5M base value derived from total capital raised and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement, yielding an implied valuation of $12M. Peer-median comparison could not be executed; while 7 same-sector peers exist, insufficient data points satisfied narrow filters (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier comparables), and cross-sector generalization would introduce material distortion. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples—the sector median across three tickers is 6.2x—remains inaccessible without disclosed revenue for Profluent, a common constraint in private company analysis.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $11M to $14M, with a median point of $12M. This range reflects the limited methodological scope available: only stage-progression modeling yielded a usable signal. Key uncertainties include the absence of comparable private company valuations at identical stage and tier, undisclosed revenue preventing public-multiple calibration, and the proxy nature of the $5M base. Validation would require additional proprietary transaction data or materialization of company-specific financial metrics.
